# Plan: monorepo-spec-roots
<!-- Generated by /hef.plan -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-05 -->

## Research Notes

- The truth map is `research.md`. Every `file:line` below is from it.
- **The launcher cannot start an app folder through `claude -w`.** A new worktree is made by `claude -w "$ID"` run
  from the repository top (`session-launch.sh:616-621`), so that session's cwd is the worktree root. For an
  app-owned item the launcher creates the worktree itself, with the same `git worktree add` that `--prepare`
  already uses (`:574-579`, moved into a shared function). It then runs `claude` from `$WT/<folder>` without `-w`.
  An item with no app keeps the `-w` path byte for byte (FR-011).
- **Size.**
  - `session-launch.sh` has 480 code lines and `status-board.sh` 488. A file that newly crosses 500 blocks the
    commit. `ledger.sh` (707) and `speckit-helper.sh` (539) are already over, so growth there is only an
    advisory, but it is still kept small.
  - The logic goes in a new library, `hooks/spec-root-lib.sh`, sourced the way `launch-item.sh` and
    `ledger-lanes.sh` already are (`session-launch.sh:51-52`, `ledger.sh:68-71`).
  - `status-board.sh` keeps only the argument parsing and dispatch for `--item-app` and `--add --app`, about
    8 lines. `item_app` and the epics walk live in the lib.
- **`spec_roots` belongs to the code repository** (plan review, 2026-11-05).
  - It is read from the entry repository's own `.claude/project-status.json`, the way the launcher asks for
    `branches` inside `TOP` (`session-launch.sh:236-243`) and `repo_config` gives it (`board-lib.sh:22`).
  - On an in-repo board that is the project's config. On an external board it is the code repository's, never
    the board repository's.
  - `status-board.sh --item-app` only checks the shape of the name: it has the board's config and cannot know
    the repository's apps. Declared-name validation happens where the repository top is known: in
    `ledger.sh record --spec-root` (the entry's repository top, the same resolution `ledger init --repo` checks
    at `ledger.sh:397`) and in the launcher (`TOP`).
- **A declared app folder with no `.specify/` is refused, never walked past** (plan review). Discovery would
  climb to the top's `.specify/` and file the app's spec there. The launcher and `--prepare` refuse when
  `$WT/$APPDIR/.specify` is missing, and name `/hef.init` from that folder.
- **`/hef.ship`** (issue #172, proposal 2) asks the app form when it creates an item in a repository with
  `spec_roots`, and writes the `app:` line through `status-board.sh --add --app <name>`. The orchestrator's form
  covers items that arrive without the line (written by hand, or created on the board).
- **Deciding the app.**
  - When `spec_roots` is declared, an item with no `app:` line gets a form (each app, plus the repository root),
    and the launcher refuses a plan launch until `spec_root` is decided.
  - `spec_root` is a declared name, `.` for the repository top, or null (undecided).
  - With no `spec_roots`, null means the top, as today.
- **Where `spec_dir` is resolved.**
  - `record_worktree` (`:348`) already makes `spec_dir` absolute. It now stores the path relative to the worktree.
    A relative outcome is read against the session's folder (`$WT/<folder>`). An absolute one under `$WT` has
    the `$WT/` prefix stripped.
  - Every reader goes through `spec_dir_abs`.
  - For an item with no app, the resolved path equals the absolute path 9.2.0 stored, so the prompts are unchanged.

## Data Model

The ledger entry gains `spec_root`: `null` (undecided, or no apps declared), `"."` (the repository top), or a
declared name.

**Migration (round 3).** An entry with `spec_dir` recorded and `spec_root` null is not undecided. This covers
every pre-9.3.0 item, and any item planned before `spec_roots` was added. `app_dir` derives its owner from
`spec_dir`: it belongs to the longest declared folder `F` such that the relative `spec_dir` starts with `F/`,
so `apps/web/.specify/…` belongs to `apps/web` and a nested `backend/api` wins over `backend`. Anything else (an
absolute 9.2.0 path, or `.specify/…`) belongs to `.`. Part 10 tests a two-segment folder and a nested pair. No form is needed and nothing deadlocks.
`list --undecided-app` lists exactly the entries a launch would refuse, in any phase: `spec_root` null and no
`spec_dir`, in a repository that declares `spec_roots`. `spec_dir` becomes relative to `worktree`; an absolute value from an older entry is kept and used
as is.

`project-status.json` gains:

```json
"spec_roots": { "backend": "backend", "frontend": "apps/web" }
```

The names match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`. A folder is relative, contains no `..` or `.` segment, is not
`.claude` or under it, and is not `.` (the top is spelled `.` only in the ledger).

## API Contracts

| Interface | Contract |
|-----------|----------|
| `spec_root_find <path>` | prints an absolute folder, exit 0. Never above `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the nearest existing folder. A `.specify` whose real path leaves the top is skipped. With no match it prints the starting folder (the nearest existing folder of `<path>`). Reads no config. |
| `spec_roots_json <repo_top>` | prints the repository's `.spec_roots` validated (FR-006) as compact JSON, `{}` when the key or the file is absent; exit 1 naming the bad entry and the expected shape. The file is `<repo_top>/.claude/project-status.json`, falling back to the main worktree's when a linked worktree has none (`.claude/` ignored, #160). This is the rule `repo_config` follows (`board-lib.sh:22-26`), copied because the guards and the helper do not source `board-lib.sh`. Every config-reading function takes the repository top as `$1`, so the three callers (ledger, launcher, board) cannot invent three conventions. |
| `spec_root_folder <repo_top> <name>` | the folder (relative) of a declared app; exit 1 naming the declared ones |
| `spec_root_names <repo_top>` | the declared names, space-separated, for messages and the forms |
| `spec_dir_abs <entry-json>` | Sketch 4; no config |
| `app_lines` | stdin item text → the values of `app:` lines (as `rfc_lines`) |
| `item_app_shape <id-label> <text>` | the one name, shape-checked only; nothing when no line (exit 0, as `--item-rfc`); two lines or a bad shape → exit 1 with the value |
| `spec_epics_all <tasks_root> <repo_top>` | the epics lines for the tasks root's `.specify/` and every declared app, app folders relative to `<repo_top>` (`$ROOT`, not `$TROOT`). On an external board (the config has a `repos` map), the app walk is skipped and the epics stay the board's own `.specify/`, as today. App-aware epics on an external board are not in 9.3.0 (docs say so). |
| `ledger.sh spec-roots <id>` · `ledger.sh list --undecided-app` | the orchestrator's form inputs (step 4) |
| `status-board.sh --item-app <id>` | `item_app_shape` on the item's body: prints the name or nothing; declared-name checks are the ledger's and the launcher's |
| `status-board.sh --add … --app <name>` | the new item's body gains `app: <name>` (shape-checked) |
| `ledger.sh record <id> --spec-root <name\|.>` | refuses an undeclared name, and refuses once `spec_dir` is set. |
| `session-launch.sh … --prepare` | a fourth line `app: <abs folder>` only when the owning root is an app |
| `speckit-helper.sh constitution` | in an app: `## Repository constitution (inherited)` + top text, then `## <app name> constitution` + app text (the declared name for the folder; its basename when undeclared); at the top or in a single-root repository: unchanged |

## Implementation Approach

1. **The library first.** Everything else calls it, and its tests pin the edge cases: FR-017 (stop at the top),
   FR-018 (nested roots), FR-019 (symlinks).
2. **The helper.**
   - A list of spec subcommands resolves the root and runs `cd` there before the `case`: `spec`, `plan`, the
     `check-*` artifact checks, `clarifications`, the checklists, `constitution`, the `list-specs*`, the phase
     markers, `req-coverage`, `mutation-*`, `arena-metrics`, `detect-stack` and `detect-test-framework`.
   - Every other subcommand (git, `rtk`, `doctor-copies`, `arena-cite-check`, `deps-*`, `check-specify-dir`)
     keeps the cwd.
   - With one `cd` up front, the 40 relative `.specify/...` lookups stay untouched. That is the smallest diff,
     and it cannot miss a lookup.
   - The helper reads `spec_roots` through `spec_roots_json "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"`. It sources the
     lib, which carries its own copy of the config rule, so it needs no `board-lib.sh`. This is used in two
     places:
     - FR-003's hint (`missing_artifact`, `speckit-helper.sh:48`) lists the top and every declared app that
       holds `.specify/specs/<branch>/`. It never walks the tree, so a monorepo's `node_modules/` and `target/`
       are left alone.
     - The constitution heading uses the declared app name, or the folder's basename when the folder is not
       declared.
   - `req-coverage --all` re-enters through `"$SELF"` instead of `"$0"` (`:418`).
   - `arena-metrics [<spec-dir>]` (`:600`) is in the `cd` list, so a path argument is read relative to the
     spec root. No caller passes one today, and the usage text says so.
3. **The guards.** One function call each. The cwd side keeps today's behaviour, and the file side adds the
   app's root.
4. **The ledger.**
   - It sources the lib.
   - `--spec-root` validates in the entry's own repository: first `cd_entry_repo "$E"` (`board-lib.sh:135`, a
     no-op on an in-repo board), then `spec_roots_json "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"`. It never uses
     `project_config`, which on an external board is the board's file (`board-lib.sh:8-10`). This is plan
     review round 2.
   - `--spec-root` takes a declared name or `.` (the repository top). `top` is a legal app name, so it is never
     a keyword.
   - Registration also reads `--item-app` (below), so an item with an `app:` line never reaches the form.
   - New subcommands for the orchestrator's form:
     - `ledger.sh spec-roots <id>` prints `{"declared": [names…], "spec_root": <value>}` from the entry's
       repository (exit 1 when none are declared);
     - `ledger.sh list --undecided-app` lists the entries a launch would refuse (Data Model, Migration).
   - `register_item` lives in `ledger-lanes.sh:14` and ends in `ledger.sh init …` (`:32`). It validates the
     `--item-app` name against `spec_roots_json` of the entry's repository BEFORE `init`: the in-repo top, or
     `.repos[$r]` from `BCTX`. This is the same "a read that fails leaves no entry" order it already uses for
     trust (`:44-46`), so an undeclared name leaves no `<id>.json` and never becomes a form (round 4). A valid
     name is then recorded with `record <id> --spec-root <name>`. Part 10 asserts that no entry exists after the
     refusal.
   - The readers take `SPEC_DIR="$(spec_dir_abs "$E")"`. A relative `--spec-dir` is refused while the entry has
     no `worktree` recorded, and `spec_dir_abs` prints nothing (never `/…`) for one written by hand.
5. **The launcher.**
   - `app_dir` (in `launch-item.sh`) returns the empty string when there is no app, so every new branch is
     behind `[ -n "$APPDIR" ]`.
   - In a plan launch, or an implement launch from `queued` (the `/hef.agent` path, `session-launch.sh:465`),
     with `spec_roots` declared and `spec_root` null, it reads `--item-app` from the hash-checked text. A
     declared name is recorded with `--spec-root`. No line is a refusal: "decide the owning app in the
     orchestrator".
   - A declared app whose `$WT/$APPDIR/.specify` is missing is refused, naming `/hef.init` from that folder.
     This holds for headless launches and `--prepare`.
6. **The board, the commands, the docs**, then the CHANGELOG.
7. **Tests.**
   - Part 10 builds a temp repository with `backend/`, `frontend/` and a top constitution. It runs the helper,
     the guards (JSON on stdin), the ledger and a launcher `--dry-run` against it.
   - The no-`spec_roots` launcher dry run is compared with a pinned fixture, `tests/fixtures/launch-920.txt`.
     It is captured from the 9.2.0 tree (`git worktree add` of `v9.2.0` in a temp folder, its whole `hooks/`)
     before any launcher change, with `$TOP`, `$ID`, `$HOME` and the time normalised (SC-003). A copy of one file
     from `main` would run against the new siblings and turn self-referential after the merge (plan review
     round 2).

## Code Sketches (Mental Alignment)

### Sketch 1: discovery
**File:** `hooks/spec-root-lib.sh` (new)
**Intent:** the git-like walk, bounded by the top, and symlink-safe.

```bash
spec_root_find() { # $1 a path (file or folder, may not exist yet) → the folder holding .specify/, else the start
  local d="$1" top real
  while [ ! -d "$d" ]; do d="$(dirname "$d")"; done; d="$(cd "$d" && pwd -P)"
  top="$(git -C "$d" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" && top="$(cd "$top" && pwd -P)" || top="$d"
  local start="$d"
  while :; do
    if [ -d "$d/.specify" ]; then real="$(cd "$d/.specify" && pwd -P)"
      case "$real/" in "$top"/*) printf '%s\n' "$d"; return 0 ;; esac; fi   # FR-019: a link out is skipped
    [ "$d" = "$top" ] || [ "$d" = / ] && break; d="$(dirname "$d")"        # FR-017: never above the top
  done
  printf '%s\n' "$start"
}
```

**Why this shape:** it is the walk the spec defines. Printing the start when nothing matches keeps today's
behaviour for a folder with no `.specify/` anywhere (`mkdir -p .specify` lands where it does now).

### Sketch 2: the helper runs from the root
**File:** `hooks/speckit-helper.sh` (modify before `case "$1"` at `:187`)

```bash
SELF="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/$(basename "$0")"   # req-coverage --all re-enters "$0" (:418): absolute before the cd
. "$(dirname "$SELF")/spec-root-lib.sh"
case "${1:-}" in
  spec|plan|check-spec|check-plan|check-artifacts|all-artifacts|clarifications|checklists*|constitution|\
  list-specs*|check-plan-review|plan-phase-*|implement-phase-*|req-coverage|mutation-*|arena-metrics|detect-stack|detect-test-framework)
    SPEC_ROOT="$(spec_root_find "$PWD")" && cd "$SPEC_ROOT" || die "speckit-helper: cannot enter the spec root of $PWD" ;;
esac
```

and the `constitution` arm:

```bash
TOPC="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)/.specify/memory/constitution.md"
if [ "$PWD" != "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" ] && [ -f "$TOPC" ]; then
  echo "## Repository constitution (inherited)"; cat "$TOPC"; [ -f .specify/memory/constitution.md ] || exit 0
  echo; echo "## $(spec_root_label "$PWD") constitution"   # the declared app name; the basename when undeclared
fi
cat .specify/memory/constitution.md 2>/dev/null || die "no constitution: …"   # unchanged message
```

**Why this shape:** one `cd` covers every relative lookup (research: about 40 of them). An explicit list keeps the
git- and path-argument subcommands where they are.

### Sketch 3: a two-sided guard
**File:** `hooks/implement-phase-test-guard.sh` (modify at `:32`); `plan-phase-write-block.sh:26` is the same shape

```bash
. "$(dirname "$0")/spec-root-lib.sh"
case "$FILE_PATH" in ""|/*) ;; *) FILE_PATH="$CWD/$FILE_PATH" ;; esac   # a relative file_path is the session's, not the hook's cwd
armed() { # $1 marker name: set in the spec root of the cwd, or of the edited file (fails closed)
  local r; for r in "$(spec_root_find "$CWD")" ${FILE_PATH:+"$(spec_root_find "$FILE_PATH")"}; do
    [ -f "$r/.specify/$1" ] && return 0; done; return 1
}
armed .implement-in-progress || exit 0
```

**Why this shape:** the cwd side is today's check (`$CWD/.specify/` is the root found from a top cwd), so a
single-root repository decides exactly as before. The file side covers a lane whose cwd moved.

### Sketch 4: the worktree-relative spec_dir
**File:** `hooks/spec-root-lib.sh`; callers `ledger.sh:550,575,849` (849 is the status column), `ledger-lanes.sh:69,103`, `session-launch.sh:222`; `hef.orchestrate.md:148` tells the orchestrator to show `<worktree>/<spec_dir>`

```bash
spec_dir_abs() { # $1 an entry (JSON) → its spec folder as an absolute path, or empty
  jq -r 'if (.spec_dir // "") == "" then empty elif (.spec_dir | startswith("/")) then .spec_dir
         elif (.worktree // "") == "" then empty else .worktree + "/" + .spec_dir end' <<<"$1"
}
```

`record_worktree` (`session-launch.sh:348`):

```bash
case "$s" in "") ;; "$WT"/*) args+=(--spec-dir "${s#"$WT"/}") ;; /*) args+=(--spec-dir "$s") ;;
  *) args+=(--spec-dir "${APPDIR:+$APPDIR/}${s#./}") ;; esac
```

**Why this shape:** an old absolute value still works (FR-010). A relative one survives a worktree move, and with
no app it resolves to the same absolute path 9.2.0 stored, so the prompts are byte-identical.

### Sketch 5: the launch in the app folder
**File:** `hooks/session-launch.sh` (modify `:205`, `:616-621`); `hooks/launch-item.sh` (`wt_add`, `app_dir`)

```bash
APPDIR="$(app_dir)" || exit 1        # "" when no app owns the item; refuses an undecided item while spec_roots is set
SPECRULE=".specify/**"; [ -z "$APPDIR" ] || SPECRULE="$APPDIR/.specify/**"
plan) ALLOWED="$(tools plan "$(jq -nc --arg a "Edit(/$TOP/.claude/worktrees/$ID/$SPECRULE)" --arg app "$APPDIR" \
   'if $app == "" then ["Read","Glob","Grep","Skill","Agent","Edit(.specify/**)","Edit(/.specify/**)",$a,"Bash(git *)"]
    else ["Read","Glob","Grep","Skill","Agent","Edit(.specify/**)",$a,"Bash(git *)"] end')")" ;;
…
if [ -n "$APPDIR" ]; then
  if [ -e "$WT" ] || [ -L "$WT" ]; then   # today's pointer check (:616, rationale :248-249) — an app item is entered no more loosely
    [ "$LANE_MODE" = 0 ] || { [ ! -L "$WT" ] && wt_branch "$WT" >/dev/null; } || die "session-launch $ROLE $ID: $WT is not a worktree of this repository (a symlink, or its git pointer was changed) — remove it and re-run"
  else wt_add die; fi
  # verify: the same check already runs on $WORKTREE (:624); it then enters "$WORKTREE/$APPDIR"
  [ -d "$WT/$APPDIR/.specify" ] || die "session-launch $ROLE $ID: app folder $APPDIR has no .specify/ in $WT — run /hef.init from $APPDIR and commit it first"
  # round 4: the folder is repository content — a committed symlink would carry the cwd, the hooks and Edit(.specify/**) out
  case "$(cd "$WT/$APPDIR" && pwd -P)/" in "$(cd "$WT" && pwd -P)"/?*) ;; *) die "session-launch $ROLE $ID: app folder $APPDIR resolves outside the worktree $WT (a link) — an app folder is a plain folder in the repository" ;; esac
  # both checks also run in --prepare and for verify on "$WORKTREE/$APPDIR"
  cd "$WT/$APPDIR" || die "session-launch $ROLE $ID: $APPDIR is not in the worktree $WT"
else …today's -w / cd "$WT" branch, unchanged…; fi
```

**Why this shape:** the `claude -w` path stays for every item with no app (FR-011). `wt_add` is the code
`--prepare` already runs, moved and not rewritten. With an app, `Edit(/.specify/**)` (the top's `.specify/`) is
dropped, so the planner cannot write the repository-level constitution.

### Sketch 6: the `app:` line
**File:** `hooks/spec-root-lib.sh`; `status-board.sh` dispatches `--item-app` to it with `body_of` + `strip_comments`

```bash
item_app_shape() { # $1 label, $2 the item text (comments stripped) → the one app name it gives; nothing when no line
  local n a; a="$(app_lines <<<"$2" | sed '/^$/d')" || true
  n="$(grep -c . <<<"$a")"; [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || return 0
  [ "$n" -eq 1 ] || { echo "$1: names $n apps — one item, one owning app" >&2; return 1; }
  [[ "$a" =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$ ]] || { echo "$1: app '$(printf '%s' "$a" | tr -cd 'a-zA-Z0-9._-' | head -c 40)' is not a name like backend" >&2; return 1; }
  printf '%s\n' "$a"
}
```

**Why this shape:** it copies `item_rfc`'s handling of untrusted text: comments stripped, one line, a strict
name, and a refusal that quotes the value safely. The declared-name check is left to the ledger and the
launcher, which know the code repository (plan review: on an external board the board's config is the wrong
file).

- **Epics:** a loop over `"$TROOT"` plus each `spec_root_folder`, with the label prefix.

## Constitution Compliance
- [x] **1. The payload never lives under `.claude/`.** The new files are `hooks/spec-root-lib.sh` and
  `tests/smoke-spec-roots.sh`, and `spec_roots` refuses `.claude` as a folder.
- [x] **2. Every command is namespaced.** No new command; `--item-app` and `--spec-root` are flags.
- [x] **3. Every guard is mutation-tested.** Part 10 has these mutants:
  - drop the file side of `armed`;
  - drop the cwd side of `armed`;
  - remove the top bound in `spec_root_find`;
  - remove the symlink check;
  - make `record --spec-root` accept an undeclared name;
  - make `app_dir` accept an undeclared name;
  - make `spec_roots_json` read the board's file on an external board;
  - drop the relative-`FILE_PATH` join in a guard;
  - let `app_dir` enter an app folder that resolves outside the worktree (a committed symlink);
  - drop the worktree pointer check on the app branch (a symlinked `$WT` for a lane-mode app item must be refused);
  - make `app_dir` refuse an entry whose `spec_dir` is recorded and `spec_root` is null (the adoption case must launch);
  - make `app_dir` return empty for an undecided item;
  - let `app_dir` accept an app folder with no `.specify/`;
  - let `spec_roots_json` accept a `..` folder, a `.claude` folder or a bad name (FR-006);
  - let `record --spec-dir` accept a path with `..` (FR-010);
  - make `spec-cite-probe` scan only the cwd's root.

  Part 10 also runs two cases on an external board: `spec_roots` read from the code repository, and the board
  repository's `spec_roots` ignored.

  The assertions are on hook exit codes and launcher dry-run output, never on data the model writes.
- [x] **4. Dependencies are zero-install.** It uses bash, jq and git, as today, and works with bash 3.2 (no
  associative arrays; `spec_roots` is read with jq).
- [x] **5. Helpers fail loudly.** These exit 1 with the value and the expected shape: an undeclared app, a bad
  `spec_roots` entry, an undecided item at launch, and a `spec_dir` with `..`. `--item-app` with no line returns
  empty at exit 0, the documented "no line" answer `--item-rfc` already gives, and the launcher treats it as a
  refusal.

## Risks & Mitigations
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| A subcommand that should not `cd` is put in the list (e.g. `arena-cite-check` reads cited paths relative to the cwd) | wrong results from the top | an explicit list, and a part 10 case per excluded subcommand run from an app folder |
| A single-root repository run from a subfolder now finds the top `.specify/` | before, it created a stray `.specify/` in the subfolder; now it uses the top | intended. CHANGELOG notes it, and a test pins it |
| `session-launch.sh` crosses 500 code lines | the commit is blocked | new logic in `launch-item.sh` and `spec-root-lib.sh`; the `--prepare` worktree code moves out (net about −10) |
| A worktree made by `git worktree add` differs from one made by `claude -w` | an app item's branch or cleanup differs | `--prepare` has used exactly this code since 9.0 for interactive lanes (`:574-579`); same branch name `worktree-$ID` |
| Claude Code started in `$WT/backend` reads project settings differently | a lane setting missed | workers get settings by `--settings` and hooks by the plugin; SC-005 live run checks it |
| Old ledger entries with an absolute `spec_dir` | must keep working | `spec_dir_abs` passes absolute values through; a part 10 case uses one |
| An interactive plan lane can write another app's `.specify/` (`plan-phase-write-block.sh:34` allows any `*/.specify/*`) | spec text lands in the wrong app | accepted for 9.3.0: the headless planner is bounded by its allowlist, and the lane's plan is reviewed by the person before build. Noted in the docs |
| `status-board.sh` crosses 500 code lines | the commit is blocked | only dispatch lines there (about 8); functions in the lib; checked before the commit |
| An untrusted `app:` line steers the cwd | limited to declared names | strict name regex, declared-only, and the body hash is checked at launch |

## Quick Start
1. Write `tests/smoke-spec-roots.sh` with the fixture repository and the `spec_root_find` cases (red), then
   `hooks/spec-root-lib.sh`.
2. The helper's `cd` list and the constitution inheritance, with tests.
3. The guards, with their mutants.
4. The ledger (`--spec-root`, `spec_dir_abs` readers), then the launcher and `--item-app`.
5. The board epics, the command text, the docs and the CHANGELOG. Then the full suite.
